newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Feb 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina will have 15 minutes every Tuesday from next week to give reply during the question-answer session in the parliament.
The cabinet on Monday approved, in principle, a proposal for setting up a national stock exchange.
Foreign Minister Abdud Samad Azad leaves on Tuesday for Kuala Lampur on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral matters with the Malayasian authorities.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Monday said that she would soon announce an anti-government agitation programme "to protect the country's independence and sovereignty".
Prime MInister Sheikh Hasina on Monday told the parliament that her governemnt wanted to make the local government institutions strong with the cooperation of the opposition.
The government has formed a nine-member committee to give recommendations to formulate new laws to check repression on women in the country.
A Japanese mission will visit Bangladesh next month to discuss new development projects under Japanese loan.
The government has appointed Syed Manzur Elahi, a leading industrialist, as honourary chairman of the Privatisation Board.
